name: Greenhaven World Server
author: otterdays
description: Greenhaven MMORPG world server (rpg-server, Rust/Axum WebSocket): one prebuilt, fully static Linux x86_64 binary. Nothing is compiled on this node and no credentials are needed - the installer downloads the release asset and verifies its SHA-256 before installing it. ONE TCP port only (WebSocket /ws and HTTP /health share it); no UDP, no query port. No config files: every setting is an environment variable, so change them as egg variables, not as files. Player data is stored in a shared PostgreSQL database (RPG_DB), so multiple world servers can share character data. Each server needs a unique RPG_WORLD_ID. Boot detection matches the line 'world listening on ws://'. Guide: server-architecture/PELICAN-EGG.md.
startup: export RPG_BIND=0.0.0.0:{{SERVER_PORT}} RPG_MAP=assets/maps/greenhaven.json RPG_DB={{RPG_DB}} RPG_WORLD_ID={{RPG_WORLD_ID}} RPG_TICK_HZ={{RPG_TICK_HZ}} ADMIN_API_TOKEN={{ADMIN_API_TOKEN}} RPG_ADMIN_BIND={{RPG_ADMIN_BIND}}; exec ./greenhaven-server

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Greenhaven world install: prebuilt static binary, no toolchain on this node.
# Safe to re-run: it replaces the binary and the map and never touches data/.
set -e
cd /mnt/server
# The release stamp is the one thing a restart cannot show you: it is rewritten on every
# install and printed at boot as the installed release.
rm -f greenhaven-release.txt
if [ -z "${RELEASE_BASE}" ]; then
  echo "RELEASE_BASE is not set. Set it to the release download prefix, for example https://github.com/<owner>/<releases-repo>/releases/download/v0.1.0"
  exit 1
fi
BIN_ASSET="greenhaven-server-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl"
MAP_ASSET="greenhaven.json"
fetch() {
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then curl -fsSL "$1" -o "$2";
  elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then wget -qO "$2" "$1";
  else echo "neither curl nor wget is present in this install image"; exit 1; fi
}
mkdir -p data assets/maps
tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
echo "Fetching ${RELEASE_BASE}/${BIN_ASSET} ..."
fetch "${RELEASE_BASE}/${BIN_ASSET}" "${tmp}/${BIN_ASSET}"
echo "Verifying the SHA-256 ..."
fetch "${RELEASE_BASE}/${BIN_ASSET}.sha256" "${tmp}/sum"
expected="$(awk '{print $1}' "${tmp}/sum")"
actual="$(sha256sum "${tmp}/${BIN_ASSET}" | awk '{print $1}')"
if [ -z "${expected}" ]; then echo "the checksum file is empty - a release must publish ${BIN_ASSET}.sha256"; exit 1; fi
if [ "${expected}" != "${actual}" ]; then echo "checksum mismatch: expected ${expected}, got ${actual}"; exit 1; fi
mv "${tmp}/${BIN_ASSET}" greenhaven-server
chmod +x greenhaven-server
echo "Fetching ${RELEASE_BASE}/${MAP_ASSET} ..."
fetch "${RELEASE_BASE}/${MAP_ASSET}" assets/maps/greenhaven.json
test -s assets/maps/greenhaven.json || { echo "the map download is empty"; exit 1; }
rm -rf "${tmp}"
test -x greenhaven-server || { echo "no executable was installed"; exit 1; }
echo "${RELEASE_BASE}" > greenhaven-release.txt
# The binary takes no CLI flags: never execute it here, it would bind a port.
echo "Install complete. The map is validated on boot; a damaged map stops the boot rather than the world."
exit 0

variables.name: Release download base
variables.description: Release download prefix (base URL). The installer fetches <RELEASE_BASE>/greenhaven-server-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, its .sha256, and <RELEASE_BASE>/greenhaven.json. To update the world, bump this string to the newer release and reinstall. Admin-only.

variables.name: PostgreSQL connection URL
variables.description: PostgreSQL connection string shared by all world servers (e.g. postgres://user:pass@host:5432/greenhaven). All player data is stored here. Admin-only, secret.

variables.name: World ID
variables.description: Unique identifier for this world server (e.g. world_1, world_2). Each server from the same egg must have a different value. Used for crash recovery and resource node scoping. Admin-only.

variables.name: Tick rate
variables.description: Simulation tick rate in Hz for this world. Default 20. Higher values mean smoother simulation but more CPU. Admin-only.

variables.name: Debug world endpoint
variables.description: 1 exposes /debug/world (live Atlas dump). Leave 0 on a public host. Admin-only.

variables.name: Admin API token
variables.description: Enables the token-gated admin API (bans, kicks, audit). Leave blank to keep it off. Use the SAME token on every world so one admin tool reaches all of them. The API binds 127.0.0.1:<port+1000> inside the container - internal only. Admin-only, secret.

variables.name: Admin API bind override
variables.description: Overrides where the admin API listens. Leave blank to use the default (127.0.0.1:<game port + 1000>, internal only). Only set this if that default collides with something else in the container. Admin-only.
